authentication.title: Access Tokens | Salesforce Help
authentication.snippet: Access tokens are your key to Salesforce APIs. When a client successfully completes an authorization flow, whether it's a standard OAuth 2.0 flow or a headless identity flow, Salesforce issues an access token that can be used to access protected Salesforce data.

authentication.title: Manage API Tokens | Salesforce Help
authentication.snippet: Use API Tokens, based on OAuth 2.0 authentication protocol, as a means to access Own from Salesforce APIs. Treat API tokens as securely as any other type of password. Make sure to store this token in a safe and secure location.

access.snippet: Supported Editions for API Access API access is enabled by default in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and Developer Edition orgs. Professional Edition orgs can add API access as an add-on. For more information, visit Salesforce Help: Add Products and Licenses with the Your Account App or contact a Salesforce account executive.

access.title: Salesforce editions with API access
access.snippet: Platform Events and the Streaming API are also available in all API-enabled editions. Not all Salesforce editions include API access. The edition your organization uses determines whether API access is available by default, can be purchased as an add-on, or is not available at all.

access.title: Manage API Access | Salesforce Help
access.snippet: Use API Access Control to manage access to your Salesforce APIs. With this feature, you can restrict all users from accessing your Salesforce APIs unless they're pre-authorized through an approved (allowlisted) connected app. Or you can restrict only customers and partners from accessing your Salesforce APIs unless they're using a connected app that is installed in your org.

webhooks.title: Get Started with Salesforce Spiff Webhook API
webhooks.snippet: A webhook provides authorized endpoints for Salesforce Spiff to sync third-party data in real time from an external source. A webhook includes a mapping that specifies how the third-party data maps to Spiff records. After you set up a webhook and define a mapping, use the Spiff webhook API endpoints to test the webhook authentication, upsert records, or delete records. 1. Create a Webhook and ...

webhooks.title: Declarative Webhooks - Effortless Integrations for Salesforce
webhooks.snippet: Quickly and easily create integrations between Salesforce and external systems. Using a point-and-click interface, users can configure webhooks to automate the transfer of data between Salesforce and other systems, eliminating the need for custom code.

webhooks.title: Create a Webhook Data Action Target | Salesforce Help
webhooks.snippet: Create a Webhook Data Action Target Send a data action event to a webhook target and protect the message integrity with a Salesforce-generated secret key. A webhook is a type of API that's event driven rather than request driven. The secret key validates the payload requests sent from Salesforce. The webhook transports the HTTP payload with events in the format of DataObjectDataChgEvent.

webhooks.title: Hooked - Declarative webhook builder for Salesforce
webhooks.snippet: Hooked is a 100% native declarative webhook builder for Salesforce. With webhooks you can automatically send JSON data from Salesforce to an external system and handle any responses.

mcp.snippet: Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers give AI agents a secure, governed way to interact with Salesforce data and automation. Think of it as a universal connector: instead of building custom API integrations ...

mcp.snippet: Salesforce Hosted MCP Servers Give AI agents a secure, governed way to interact with Salesforce data and automation using the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Any compatible AI client can connect to your org using standard OAuth authentication.

mcp.title: Salesforce DX MCP Server | Salesforce Help
mcp.snippet: The Salesforce DX MCP Server is a specialized Model Context Protocol (MCP) implementation that facilitates interaction between LLMs and Salesforce orgs. Use the DX MCP Server and its tools to enter natural language prompts in your IDE to execute standard DX tasks, such as syncing metadata, running Apex and agent tests, and creating scratch orgs.

mcp.title: Connecting MCP Servers to Salesforce
mcp.snippet: The process for connecting Salesforce to an MCP server depends on the source of the server. Connect third-party MCP servers using the Agentforce Registry. Connect Mulesoft and Salesforce-hosted servers using API Catalog.
